chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Arzmee, who said:

I was sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in the chamber (Hijr) under the gutter. A man was disputing with another man, and one of them was saying to his companion, 'By Allah, I do not know from where the wind blows.' When he repeated this many times, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'So do you know?' He said, 'No, but I hear the people saying it.' So I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, from where does the wind blow?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, the wind is captive under this Shami (Syrian) corner. So when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, intends to bring something out of it, He brings it out: either the South (wind), so it is the South; or the North (wind), so it is the North; or Saba (wind), so it is Saba; and Dabour (wind), so it is Dabour.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'Among the signs of that is that you will always see this corner moving constantly, in winter and summer, and night and day.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الشَّامِيُّ: The Shami (Syrian) corner of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: Where do the winds originate according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the cosmological mechanism of wind, describing it as being bound beneath the Shami corner of the Kaaba and released by divine command into the four cardinal directions. This narration is often cited by Shia scholars to illustrate the tangible connection between the Kaaba and natural phenomena, serving as a sign (*ayah*) of Allah's power over creation. The mention of the corner's constant movement provides a physical indicator of the spiritual and metaphysical forces at work.

en.hubeali: H 14849 – Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from one of his companions, from Muhammad Al-Fazl, from Arzamy who said:

I was seated with Abu Abdullahasws in the chamber underneath the shade and a man was disputing with a man, and one of them was saying to his companion, ‘By Allahazwj, I do not know from where the wind blows’. So when he said it many times, Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘So do you know?’ He said, ‘No, but I heard the people talking about it’. So I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws, from where does the wind blow?’ Heasws said: ‘It is captivated under this Al-Shamy corner. So if Allahazwj Intends that Heazwj Takes something out of it, Heazwj Takes it out, whether it is the South (wind) so it is the South, and whether it is the North (wind) so it is the North, and Saba (wind) so it is the Saba, and Dabour (wind) so it is the Dabour’. Then heasws said: ‘From the signs of that is that you will never stop seeing this corner moving ever, in the winter, and the summer, and the night, and the day’.

So when he said it many times, Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said: ‘So do you know?’ He said, ‘No, but I heard the people talking about it’. So I said to Abu Abdullah (a.s.), ‘May I be sacrificed for you (a.s.), from where does the wind blow?’ He (a.s.) said: ‘It is captivated under this Al-Shamy corner. So if Allah (azwj) Intends that He (azwj) Takes something out of it, He (azwj) Takes it out, whether it is the South (wind) so it is the South, and whether it is the North (wind) so it is the North, and Saba (wind) so it is the Saba, and Dabour (wind) so it is the Dabour’.
